rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 1 of 4, about 15 m, trending slightly left to a larger tree.
rappel_detail.station: The slung tree at the top of the route.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 2 of 4, about 55 m, into the left side of the right-hand cave. Then walk right to the bolted anchor above pitch 2.
rappel_detail.station: The larger tree below and left of the top.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 3 of 4, about 50 m, down and right.
hazards: Diagonal: you have to steer to stay on line for the next anchor.
rappel_detail.station: The bolted anchor above pitch 2, reached by walking right in the cave.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 4 of 4, about 40 m, to the narrow ledge at the base.
rappel_detail.station: The next bolted anchor down and right.

wa_the_l_h_route_free_variation.rappels: Rappel the Ellen Pea line: 4 rappels on two 60 m ropes (about 15, 55, 50 and 40 m), or walk off to the west
wa_the_l_h_route_free_variation.rappel_count_note: This route descends Ellen Pea’s rappel line. Four rappels on two 60 m ropes: every rappel needs both ropes. Nearly every anchor is bolted below the top trees, and some rappels are diagonal, so steer to stay on line. About an hour from the top to the base. Instead of rappelling, you can traverse off to a 3rd-class ramp partway down.
wa_the_l_h_route_free_variation.descent_text: From the top, rappel down the Ellen Pea line using two ropes (diagonal rappelling is required in places), or walk down via the 3rd-class terrain to the west.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 1 of 7, about 35 m on two 70 m ropes, angling left to the ledge atop pitch 10.
rappel_detail.station: From an anchor on the right edge of the highest summit overhangs.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 2 of 7, about 30 m on two 70 m ropes, down the flake pitch.
Rappel 3 of 7, about 40 m on two 70 m ropes, angling hard right; fixed wires are in place for directionals on the strand you will not pull.
rappel_detail.station: From the anchor below the flake pitch.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 4 of 7, about 45 m on two 70 m ropes, into the cave.
Rappel 5 of 7, about 61 m on two 70 m ropes, a rope-stretching rappel to the ledge atop pitch 3.
hazards: This one stretches two 70 m ropes; knot the ends.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 6 of 7, about 45 m on two 70 m ropes, down pitch 3.
Rappel 7 of 7, about 60 m on two 70 m ropes, down and slightly right over the terrain of pitches 1 and 2.
rappel_detail.station: From the anchor at the foot of pitch 3.

wa_the_tiger.rappels: 7 rappels on two 70 m ropes down the route; or scramble off down and left on a treed ramp into the 3rd-class gully, or rappel the Ellen Pea line
wa_the_tiger.rappel_count_note: Seven rappels on two 70 m ropes, one of them a rope-stretching 61 m from the cave. A non-rappel descent tops out and scrambles down and left on a treed ramp into the 3rd-class gully left of the wall. From the base, walk left down the gully, or rappel the bolted slab below and right: about 75 m more, on three bolted anchors.

wa_hourglass_gully_winter.rappels: 2-3 raps (two 30 m ropes) from the upper gully/East Ridge down to roughly the saddle above Lake Serene; anchors are typically slung trees, horns, or pickets rather than fixed hardware.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 1 of 2, double-rope (two 60 m ropes), down the West Face to the base of the black basalt dike. Then scramble several hundred feet of Class 3 down the dike to the top of the crux dihedral.
rappel_detail.anchor: large horn thickly slung with rappel webbing, about 50 ft below the true summit
rappel_detail.station: Belay and downclimb the exposed summit ridge back to the large slung horn about 50 ft below the top, a good confirmation that you are on the descent.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 2 of 2, a diagonal double-rope rappel that reaches the snow finger in one go.
rappel_detail.anchor: natural anchor (slung horn, block or chockstone) at the top of the crux dihedral
hazards: The last person down should place a directional piece so the rope runs true on the diagonal.
rappel_detail.station: The top of the crux dihedral, reached by scrambling down the dike.

wa_gunsight_peak_standard.rappels: 2 double-rope (2x60 m) rappels down the West Face, separated by belayed downclimbing of the summit ridge and several hundred feet of Class 3 on the dike
wa_gunsight_peak_standard.rappel_count_note: A four-station sequence of 50/50/50/20 m is sometimes attached to this route. It matches, figure for figure, the descent of north Gunsight Peak's West Face — a 5.11+, 6-pitch, 600 ft rock route on a different summit — and does not belong to this Class 5.6 glacier route on the main spire. Nothing about those figures was measured here, so they are not carried. What is documented for this route is two double-rope rappels: after belaying back down the exposed summit ridge, one double-rope rappel down the west face, then a diagonal double-rope rappel, with directional protection placed along the way, that reaches the snow finger in one go. That descent used two 60 m ropes. No single-rope descent of this route is documented.
wa_gunsight_peak_standard.descent_text: Reverse the ridge crest from the summit: belay/downclimb the exposed summit ridge back down to a large horn about 50' below the true summit that is thickly slung with rappel webbing (a good on-route confirmation marker). From there, make a double-rope (60m x 2) rappel down the West Face to regain the base of the route's black basaltic dike/dihedral. Scramble down several hundred feet of Class 3 terrain on the dike to the top of the crux dihedral, then make a second, diagonal double-rope (60m x 2) rappel — the last person down should place a directional piece of protection to keep the rope running true — which in one pull reaches the snow finger below. From the snow finger, downclimb or glissade back onto the Chikamin Glacier and reverse the approach (re-climb to the Chikamin-Dome col, cross the Dome Glacier, over Itswoot Pass/Cub Pass, down Bachelor Meadows/Bachelor Creek, and out Downey Creek Trail #768) to the trailhead. All anchors reported on this route are natural — slung horns, blocks, and chockstones — with no fixed/bolted stations, consistent with its remote, low-traffic character. Typical parties use two 60m ropes for both rappels; expect the crux dihedral's black rock to be loose in spots, and factor in real crevasse-travel time and daylight for the long glacier return to camp.
